name: Voter Action Project HQ
subject: This is a terrible SCOTUS decision
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Integrity First Voter Action Project, www
body:
Knocking out Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act is going to reconstitute state legislatures, city councils, judicial districts, and every other type of political boundary in which racial minorities will be cut off from having a voice in their government. Louisiana, Alabama, and other states guilty of racial gerrymandering in the past have already pushed to restart the practice in the courts in the wake of this case.
This decision will silence untold numbers of voters and spiral our fight for voting rights back sixty years. RUSH $35 or more right now to help fight for the values the VRA stood for and defend our fundamental right to vote >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=050326_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
MJ: Supreme Court Deals a Death Blow to the Voting Rights Act [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=050326_3&amount=25]
Team: The Supreme Court’s six-to-three conservative majority issued a staggering ruling yesterday that essentially kills the remaining protections of the Voting Rights Act , dealing a death blow to the country’s most important civil rights law.
The majority opinion by Justice Samuel Alito in Louisiana v. Callais strikes down the congressional map in Louisiana and in doing so " narrows Section 2 of the VRA to the point of irrelevance, making it nearly impossible to prove that a gerrymandered map violates the right of voters of color ."
The impact shows how partisan this all is. This decision harms only one political party to the direct benefit of the other and return parts of the country to a suppressive era we thought we left behind sixty years ago.
What can we do to respond? It sounds simple, but just get back to work informing voters, reengaging lapsed voters, registering new ones, and turning out everyone we can for the midterms and beyond.
Team: We need everyone's help, now more than ever. Step up with $35 or whatever you can today and help us defend the right to vote >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=050326_3&amount=35]

Justice Elena Kagan forcefully dissented. “ I dissent because the Court’s decision will set back the foundational right Congress granted of racial equality in electoral opportunity, ” she wrote.
University of Florida political scientist Michael McDonald also pointed out, “ my quick read of Callais decision is that the majority says if a racial community votes consistently with a party, then it is okay to deny them representation because that’s just partisan gerrymandering .”
The consequences are simple to understand and grave for voter participation. The more vengeful partisans make voter participation feel worthless, the less people actually take part. Needless to say, the less people who participate, the less our democracy and our government looks like the people it's supposed to represent.
It was clear long before the MAGA movement that Chief Justice Roberts has seen the removal of the VRA as one of his top goals for his time on the Court. After decades of different cases, yesterday he seemed to finally succeed.
We simply refuse to let our democracy go backwards like this. Will you chip in with $35 or more to stand with us against these partisan efforts to silence voters? >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=050326_3&amount=35]

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

| | Peter,

My name is Katie Britt, and if it’s alright with you, I’d like to share a little about who I am. **I’m not part of the D.C. cocktail circuit, and I never will be._That’s just not who I am._**

In 2022, I was elected to represent the great state of Alabama in the United States Senate. I became the first woman in Alabama’s history to hold this seat—but that’s not why I ran.

I ran because I’m a _**mom**_ , a _**wife**_ , and a _**conservative**_ who’s fed up with the direction this country is heading. I came to Washington to fight for our families, to protect our values, and to bring some Alabama backbone to a broken system.

I’ve lived a life full of hard work, determination, and breaking barriers. There have been challenges and triumphs alike, but I wouldn’t trade any of it.

My story is a testament to what America stands for—the American Dream. From a small town in Alabama, I rose to become my state’s U.S. Senator—a woman who’s breaking barriers and fighting for conservative values every day.

__**I’m living proof of the limitless opportunity and freedom that define this country.**__

But, I didn’t get here by playing it safe or staying quiet, **and I’m not about to start now.**

The radical Left wants to _silence_ conservatives like me. They want to drown out our voices and push their agenda without opposition, but I’m standing firm.

I’m fighting tooth and nail to keep up and push back hard, for Alabama, for our values, and for every American who believes in freedom.

clean_body: From my heart to yours, Peter. | | | | | Peter, My name is Katie Britt, and if it’s alright with you, I’d like to share a little about who I am. I’m not part of the D.C. cocktail circuit, and I never will be.That’s just not who I am. In 2022, I was elected to represent the great state of Alabama in the United States Senate. I became the first woman in Alabama’s history to hold this seat—but that’s not why I ran. I ran because I’m a mom , a wife , and a conservative who’s fed up with the direction this country is heading. I came to Washington to fight for our families, to protect our values, and to bring some Alabama backbone to a broken system. I didn’t come here to make friends with the political elite. I came here to stand up for the people who don’t have a voice in the room—and I’m not backing down. Before coming to the Senate, I served as the first female president and CEO of the Business Council of Alabama, and before that, I was Chief of Staff to Senator Richard Shelby. I’ve never shied away from a challenge—and I’ve never forgotten who I’m fighting for. In every role I’ve held, my mission has been the same: deliver real results for Alabama families and the American people. Before starting my career in public service, I earned my undergraduate and law degrees from the University of Alabama. That experience taught me how to lead, think on my feet, and fight for what I believe in—and it laid the foundation for everything I’ve done since. But long before that, I was just a small-town girl from Enterprise, Alabama. My dad ran the local hardware store. My mom taught dance to almost every kid in town. We didn’t grow up with wealth or political connections. We came from hard work, grit, and doing things the right way.That’s how I was raised, and that’s exactly how I lead. My husband Wesley and our two amazing kids are my rock. In 2011, a tornado tore through our home and nearly took our lives. That moment changed everything, and reminded me what truly matters. Faith , family , and resilience. I’ve lived a life full of hard work, determination, and breaking barriers. There have been challenges and triumphs alike, but I wouldn’t trade any of it. My story is a testament to what America stands for—the American Dream. From a small town in Alabama, I rose to become my state’s U.S. Senator—a woman who’s breaking barriers and fighting for conservative values every day. I’m living proof of the limitless opportunity and freedom that define this country. But, I didn’t get here by playing it safe or staying quiet, and I’m not about to start now. The radical Left wants to silence conservatives like me. They want to drown out our voices and push their agenda without opposition, but I’m standing firm. I’m fighting tooth and nail to keep up and push back hard, for Alabama, for our values, and for every American who believes in freedom. The support I’ve received so far means everything, but this fight is far from over. We need the resources to keep going strong and hold our ground. Thank you, and may God bless America. # [Please Vote for Me to Represent US!](https://bethfarnhamforcongress.com/2026/05/03/please-vote-for-me-to-represent-us/?jetpack_skip_subscription_popup)
---
By **Elizabeth Farnham** on May 3, 2026
---
| **District Round-up 05.03.26**
---
Dear Neighbor, Thank you for reading my District Round-up. As your candidate for Pennsylvania’s 13th Congressional District, it is my honor and pleasure to deliver to you where I’ve been and what issues I’ve tackled in the past week. Criss-crossing the counties of Adams, Franklin, Fulton, Bedford, Cambria, Blair, Huntingdon, Mifflin, Juniata, Perry, Cumberland, and Somerset gives me great opportunities to meet with voters, hear what is on your hearts and minds, and the chance to voice my fight for Everyday Americans. If you would like to contribute to my campaign, please donate here:**[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/beth-farnham-for-congress-1](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=8292e16c49b2e6bc59524058500ece4a585dfca38d5acca3857a176202c4b62b&blog_id=213069660&post_id=7227&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=9ba0515e7c9363236a0ec6a27795a9b0&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYWN0Ymx1ZS5jb20vZG9uYXRlL2JldGgtZmFybmhhbS1mb3ItY29uZ3Jlc3MtMQ=&email_id=5d8c72705e7c783fe39f4352c91321e3)**
---
| **Please Vote for Me!**
---
By now, you should have received your mail-in ballot if you signed up to vote that way. **For all Democrats** – I am on the Democratic ballot to vote for. **For all Republicans** – you are welcome to write my name in and darken the corresponding oval instead of voting for John Joyce. **Please spread the word.**
---
To All Who Made This Ballot Possible – THANK YOU
---
Thank you for giving us a chance at real representation.
---
Thank you for believing in a system of checks and balances.
---
Thank you for forging a path of accountability for a rogue president, his prejudiced administration, racist Supreme Court Justices, and ultra-wealthy Members of Congress who have abandoned their jobs.
---
Thank you for fighting for Reproductive Freedom.
---
Thank you for wanting to establish Affordability of our gas, groceries, and light bills.
---
Thank you for battling for Universal Healthcare.
---
Thank you for caring to feed the hungry.
---
Thank you for defending Public Education.
---
Thank you for demanding to abolish ICE.
---
Thank you for being a steward of the Earth.
---
Thank you for standing with me.
---
Thank you for supporting my candidacy.
---
Together, we [#ChooseDemocracy](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=b121f717cfd63ebe979aaac26fa7e7c0486ccb8a9172c022270adabdfe39b781&blog_id=213069660&post_id=7227&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=e75b831b7ed83965dc6fb4f5e6476b57&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_&email_id=5d8c72705e7c783fe39f4352c91321e3) !
---
| |
---
| |
---
| | **Endorsements Alert!**
---
Thank you South Central Young Democrats!
---
I am proud to be endorsed by these progressive young people.
---
Together, we [#ChooseDemocracy](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=556ffa1c161476c21ba441950bc3cc098f77dd61821044f484aa524d55dc1bea&blog_id=213069660&post_id=7227&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=ee2378ad096e331fbc6944c679feb9bb&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_&email_id=5d8c72705e7c783fe39f4352c91321e3) !
---
| |
---
Many thanks to the [Perry County Democrats](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=36aa80dbb50872e3ac83e3564bc891000c9d7ffa96f04a449ea113b01595ff84&blog_id=213069660&post_id=7227&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=fd9a75a23d422cfdf12914aeb7aa8248&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_&email_id=5d8c72705e7c783fe39f4352c91321e3) for their unanimous endorsement of my campaign. I appreciate all they do for Perry County residents.
---
Their letter reads:
---
On April 19th, the Perry County Democratic Committee unanimously endorsed Beth Farnham for U.S. House of Representatives for Congressional District 13. Beth is a passionate, determined and intelligent person who ran previously in 2024 for this position. She is consistent in her messaging about what the working class has been anxious to hear. Beth will defend public education, vote to raise the minimum wage to a living wage, support and strengthen gun safety laws, reduce the cost of healthcare and will work to reduce the high cost of food and other essentials we need. Most importantly, Beth will work for us, not those who are elected but never “represent” what the people want! We highly recommend voting for Beth Farnham for U.S. House of Representatives for Congressional District 13! She’s one of us!
---
| |
---
Together, we [#ChooseDemocracy](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=b23dc1168aff341eec2acb2d91556f86b0f1f49bdaed269701e4f72c3fcb3086&blog_id=213069660&post_id=7227&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=acca45123a89559aa5b94480bfcdbe7e&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_&email_id=5d8c72705e7c783fe39f4352c91321e3)
---
| **How You Can Help Bring US Representative John Joyce to Debate Me**
---
Why won’t my opponent, US Representative and multimillionaire, John Joyce, debate me?
---
Because he represents the ultra-wealthy, not Everyday Americans.
---
It’s why he voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act – it strips away healthcare from the poorest among us, dramatically increases premiums of Pennie (Affordable Care Act in Pennsylvania), and forces cuts to Medicare.
---
By extending the 2017 tax cuts to the ultra-wealthy, the national deficit will skyrocket, mandating at least $418 billion dollars to be cut from Medicare, forcing senior citizens to pay more out-of-pocket.
---
He doesn’t care that Trump’s never-ending war is costing Americans $1 billion/day.
---
He doesn’t care that Trump puts our national security at risk with decreased weapons.
---
He doesn’t care about rising prices of gasoline, groceries, or light bills.
---
Joyce doesn’t care that his vote for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act strips food assistance from his hungriest constituents.
---
He doesn’t care that his vote for the Save America Act strips voting rights primarily from women.
---
He doesn’t care that mothers needing life-saving D&C’s, mislabled “abortion” in several states are denied them after miscarriage, only to die of sepsis later.
---
The moment he opens his mouth to defend his awful positions is the moment he bares his ugly, tortured soul.
---
And then, you’ll realize that he never cared about you.
---
So he’ll stay hidden, in the shadows, avoiding in-person Town Halls, forgoing fora, and dodging debates.
---
But you can change this.
---
Call upon your county Chamber of Commerce, instutitions of higher learning, newspapers, and television stations.
---
Demand to hear your candidates for US Congress debate their postions at the venue of their choice.
---
And require from them that even if one candidate, the cowardly John Joyce, doesn’t show up, the host will still ask the important questions of the present candidate, i.e. me, Beth Farnham.
---
Because you choose Democratic norms.
---
You choose Transparency.
---
You choose Real Representation.
---
You [#ChooseDemocracy](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=061fe2dce8f5726215f5e2829ff45b7365b56e8ac9d0a4c8ba2a8e00fa73a6a9&blog_id=213069660&post_id=7227&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=8319e9362d000fdabb3582dbdfffa949&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_&email_id=5d8c72705e7c783fe39f4352c91321e3)
---

| **Candidate Forum #1**
---
Many thanks to the Franklin County Democratic Committee for hosting the Candidate Forum on Wednesday evening.
---
Thank you also to everyone who attended.
---
There was much interest on candidate positions regarding AI Data Centers and I.C.E.
---
Together, we [#ChooseDemocracy](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=d1b3595dbe2408ff60f2f862138837254b5ca570c9000088aa7a3b531df693f5&blog_id=213069660&post_id=7227&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=0199f1f3b396596ec2697d0c0bb99978&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_&email_id=5d8c72705e7c783fe39f4352c91321e3) and Community!

| **Supporting Local Businesses**
---
Wednesday afternoon, the Cinco de Mayo meet and greet at the Volvo in Shippensburg was the place to be!
---
Hosted by the Greater Chambersburg Chamber of Commerce, owners and workers alike met to discuss the issues near and dear to their hearts.
---
I met a number of voters including Mike Davidson and also ran into Commissioner Bob Ziobrowski!
---
Small businesses are one of the heartbeats of America but they are especially affected by healthcare costs which is why I’m proud to tell them that I support a national healthcare plan as well as The Rule of Two.
---
Together, we [#ChooseDemocracy](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=67014f02ea328845fa9b72fc0199106e2d1ce525e166ff3cbee9828ee8c982c9&blog_id=213069660&post_id=7227&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=213a810d3e1236074603b57cf4fe00d4&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_&email_id=5d8c72705e7c783fe39f4352c91321e3) and entrepreneurship!

| |

Great crowd|

| **Candidate Forum #2**
---
Many thanks to the Blair County Democratic Committee for, along with the Blair County Young Democrats, chair Owen Smith Meyer, for hosting a great candidate forum at the AFL-CIO Union Building in Altoona on Friday afternoon. It was a great session of candidate passion and voter engagement. I was happy to participate with candidates Caleb McCoy for PA State 79th District, Sarah Holland for PA State 80th District, and Sean Steeg PA Senate 30th District.
---
Together, we Choose Democracy!

| **Spring Brunch** **and Doorknocking**
---
Many thanks to the Cambria County Democratic Committee for inviting me to speak at their Spring Brunch on Saturday at the Parkway Diner in Portage. It was refreshing to reconnect with such dedicated Democrats in this pivotal election year. Later, I went doorknocking in Portage and connected with several more voters.
---
2026 is our year!
---
Together, we Choose Democracy!
---

---
With Eugene Depasquale at the Cambria Dems brunch.
---
| **Charity of the Week!**
---
Please support The Arc of Cumberland & Perry Counties (CPARC) , if you can.
---
Their mission is to “...empower, inspire, and educate people with intellectual and developmental disabilities, their families, and the community.”
---
Besides services like housing, adult daycare, Advocacy, and education, CPARC also partners with The Sassy Gourmet which employs people with disabilities.
---
Their website is here: [https://cparc.org/support-us/](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=c002101f20f5f638bdf146d16c6cbd4366b17f66afb84ea1b9f5ceb1cf5a7693&blog_id=213069660&post_id=7227&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=182a051a933065deb5281987ba733bcf&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly9jcGFyYy5vcmcvc3VwcG9ydC11cy8&email_id=5d8c72705e7c783fe39f4352c91321e3)

| **Comparing and Contrasting Votes on Legislation**
---
Check out how Joyce recently voted, how I would have voted in comparison, and why!
---
---

As your candidate for Pennsylvania’s 13th Congressional District, it is my honor and pleasure to deliver to you where I’ve been and what issues I’ve tackled in the past week. Criss-crossing the counties of Adams, Franklin, Fulton, Bedford, Cambria, Blair, Huntingdon, Mifflin, Juniata, Perry, Cumberland, and Somerset gives me great opportunities to meet with voters, hear what is on your hearts and minds, and the chance to voice my fight for Everyday Americans. If you would like to contribute to my campaign, please donate here: | Please Vote for Me! By now, you should have received your mail-in ballot if you signed up to vote that way. For all Democrats – I am on the Democratic ballot to vote for. For all Republicans – you are welcome to write my name in and darken the corresponding oval instead of voting for John Joyce. Please spread the word. To All Who Made This Ballot Possible – THANK YOU Thank you for giving us a chance at real representation. Thank you for believing in a system of checks and balances. Thank you for forging a path of accountability for a rogue president, his prejudiced administration, racist Supreme Court Justices, and ultra-wealthy Members of Congress who have abandoned their jobs. Thank you for fighting for Reproductive Freedom. Thank you for wanting to establish Affordability of our gas, groceries, and light bills. Thank you for battling for Universal Healthcare. Thank you for caring to feed the hungry. Thank you for defending Public Education. Thank you for demanding to abolish ICE. Thank you for being a steward of the Earth. Thank you for standing with me. Thank you for supporting my candidacy. Together, we ! | | | | | | Endorsements Alert! Thank you South Central Young Democrats! I am proud to be endorsed by these progressive young people. Together, we ! | | Many thanks to the for their unanimous endorsement of my campaign. I appreciate all they do for Perry County residents. Their letter reads: On April 19th, the Perry County Democratic Committee unanimously endorsed Beth Farnham for U.S. House of Representatives for Congressional District 13. Beth is a passionate, determined and intelligent person who ran previously in 2024 for this position. She is consistent in her messaging about what the working class has been anxious to hear. Beth will defend public education, vote to raise the minimum wage to a living wage, support and strengthen gun safety laws, reduce the cost of healthcare and will work to reduce the high cost of food and other essentials we need. Most importantly, Beth will work for us, not those who are elected but never “represent” what the people want! We highly recommend voting for Beth Farnham for U.S. House of Representatives for Congressional District 13! She’s one of us! | | Together, we | How You Can Help Bring US Representative John Joyce to Debate Me Why won’t my opponent, US Representative and multimillionaire, John Joyce, debate me? Because he represents the ultra-wealthy, not Everyday Americans. It’s why he voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act – it strips away healthcare from the poorest among us, dramatically increases premiums of Pennie (Affordable Care Act in Pennsylvania), and forces cuts to Medicare. By extending the 2017 tax cuts to the ultra-wealthy, the national deficit will skyrocket, mandating at least $418 billion dollars to be cut from Medicare, forcing senior citizens to pay more out-of-pocket. He doesn’t care that his vote for the Save America Act strips voting rights primarily from women. He doesn’t care that mothers needing life-saving D&C’s, mislabled “abortion” in several states are denied them after miscarriage, only to die of sepsis later. The moment he opens his mouth to defend his awful positions is the moment he bares his ugly, tortured soul. And then, you’ll realize that he never cared about you. Demand to hear your candidates for US Congress debate their postions at the venue of their choice. And require from them that even if one candidate, the cowardly John Joyce, doesn’t show up, the host will still ask the important questions of the present candidate, i.e. me, Beth Farnham. This district is rated “Lean D” and is one we must win in order to retake the House Majority this November.
But now, there’s a real risk Republicans could hold the seat... perhaps even by locking Democrats out of the general election entirely by taking BOTH top spots in June’s primary.
That would be a disaster. And it means we have to act immediately .
The California Democratic Party is already organizing in CA-48 — knocking doors, calling voters, and building the grassroots operation we need to win.
But this poll changes everything.
We need to TURBO-CHARGE our organizing efforts right now to make sure Democrats break through and secure a spot in the general election. I'm a pediatrician. I’m pissed. I’m scared. And I need your help to defeat Lindsey Graham in the U.S. Senate.
I’m not the “monsters-under-the-bed” kind of scared. I’m the “I’ve watched children suffer from preventable illness and injury while politicians do absolutely nothing” kind of scared.
I’ve treated kids who’ve been shot. Kids whose families struggle to afford their medications.
Kids who live with mold that causes asthma attacks, miss school for climate disasters, and watch politicians use them as political pawns.
And now? Trump is causing chaos and Lindsey Graham is right by his side.
And Medicaid — the program that keeps half our pediatric patients insured, healthy, and...alive — is on the chopping block to pay for tax breaks for billionaires.
So yeah, I never planned to run for Senate.
But I’m scared. I’m pissed. I’m motivated. And I’m 100% in.
I’m running for Senate in South Carolina to defeat Lindsey Graham and to fight for the kids no one in D.C. seems to be thinking about. So I need you with me.
We need to hit 10,000 donations before midnight to prove that this campaign can go the distance. Can I count on you to split a donation with my campaign and Resist Reclaim Rebuild? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-annieandrews]

I’m running because the Republican Party, led by people like Lindsey Graham, is dismantling the very systems that keep our kids safe here in South Carolina.
I’m running because the issues I care about — children’s healthcare, vaccines, gun violence, public education, Social Security, Medicaid and Medicare — are under direct attack right now.
And I’m running because I consider it my professional duty as a pediatrician — to give children a strong voice at the national level. Too many are comfortable on the sidelines. That won’t work for me.
We need bold leaders who aren’t afraid to fight. I am ready.
Even though the path will be hard, I know Lindsey Graham must be held accountable. He certainly doesn’t deserve a free pass back to D.C. for six more years.

A few years ago, the United Nations adopted a framework called the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples. It took over 25 years in international forums, far from the kitchen tables of British Columbia (BC), to be drafted. In 2019, however, the provincial legislature in Victoria unanimously [converted the global framework into binding BC law](https://substack.com/redirect/1c78fab3-40b7-41bd-90ee-c026f8c23d4b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Most legislators thought they were making a symbolic statement of good intent. Instead, they were threading a needle through the load-bearing seams of BC's historical legal and economic order.
Last August, [after the longest trial in Canadian history](https://substack.com/redirect/497dd44b-ce41-4ae2-893c-ab8cd1c60732?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a BC Supreme Court judge declared that 3.25 square kilometers of Richmond (the fourth largest municipality in the province and home to almost a quarter million residents) sit atop land that is owned by the Cowichan Tribes. Specifically, the court found the homes, farms, and industrial sites on that land fall under Aboriginal title, deeming that historical and current grants of fee-simple ownership were defective. Stop and read that again. _The court ruled that those who live on the Cowichan land must now worry about whether they own the home they paid for and think they own_.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/421a882c-59cb-468f-b975-29ef556c7cfd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Four months later, the Court of Appeal struck down the province's mineral tenure system, ruling that it failed to incorporate First Nation perspectives. DRIPA's language, the court ruled, was "obligatory and imperative" and mandated that First Nations be consulted. This ruling, known as the Gitxalla decision, has put a chill over the entire sector and introduced paralyzing uncertainty.
Facing a firestorm of concern from everyone, Premier David Eby tried in January to suspend parts of DRIPA to hold the system together. By April, after fierce opposition, he withdrew the proposal. The challenge of addressing First Nation claims is a loose thread of BC society. If the politics pull with enough force, the sweater will unravel.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/22e0a58a-a912-4c4b-a9b4-526a277fe99a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This is a story about how a global framework, adopted without sufficient democratic deliberation, is now reshaping property rights, investment flows, and the social contract of an entire province. As an outsider who has spoken with several dozen elected officials in Canada, I've come to a simple conclusion: _**The only way out of this mess is forward, through growth, not backward, through litigation**_.
First, we must acknowledge the difficult truth. British Columbia's Indigenous peoples (~5% of the population) were dispossessed of their lands without treaties across most of the territory. The historical injustice is real, documented, and ongoing in its effects. Anyone arguing otherwise isn't engaging with facts. Reconciliation is both a moral and a practical necessity. The question is not whether to reconcile, but how. And I think the current path is misguided. Rather than helping move society forward, it's poised to transfer one community's grievances to another.

Here's another truth worth accepting. A new legal regime is now allowing a collective claim asserted by 5% of the population to undermine and cloud the fee-simple title of the other 95%. Homeowners in Richmond, for instance, who purchased their properties in good faith decades ago now read newspaper headlines wondering whether their deeds are valid. Mining juniors who staked claims under provincial law now find those claims legally questionable.
The collectivist logic embedded in the UN-inspired framework is that historical group rights can supersede individual property rights. This approach is colliding with a foundational liberal premise that an individual's title, lawfully acquired, is secure. This is not a minor legal dispute. **It is a fundamental question about what kind of society British Columbia is going to be.**

In South Africa, an elegant constitutional framework promised both property protection and historical restitution. Three decades on, neither has been delivered. The land-reform process bogged down in proceduralism; promised redistribution was never realized; political legitimacy is now eroding into talk of expropriation without compensation. _**My take: half-measures don 't work and are likely to embitter everyone.**_
In Colombia, the 2016 peace agreement with the FARC ended fifty years of armed conflict. Ten years into a fifteen-year implementation timeline, rural land reform is far behind schedule, more than five hundred former combatants have been killed, and successive governments whiplash between commitment and rollback. _**My take: announcements are easy; sustained institutional follow-through is difficult.**_
While every situation is unique, there seems to be one overarching conclusion I've drawn from my study of these (and other) cases. When reconciliation processes get bogged down in dividing today's economic pie, everyone loses. But When the focus is on the generation of broad-based growth, the politics become manageable.

Which brings me to the opportunity emerging from today's global uncertainty...and the only strategy that I believe can hold BC's fractious society together. **It 's time to stop fighting over slices and bake a much bigger pie.**
Let's not forget that while British Columbia has been litigating, the world has been re-pricing its demand for goods BC can deliver. Three demand shocks have arrived simultaneously, and each represents a generational opportunity for the province if it moves quickly enough to capture them.
First, let's explore the impact of the Iran war. Since February's strikes and Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz, Asian spot LNG prices have spiked more than 140% above pre-war levels. The IEA has called it "the greatest threat to global energy security in history." Asian importers (Japan, Korea, China, India, etc.) are now urgently seeking what they call "secure" LNG supply. What's "secure"? Cargoes from politically stable democracies, on routes that don't pass through the Persian Gulf. British Columbia's North Coast sits closer to Asian markets than any other major LNG-exporting jurisdiction on Earth. The window to lock in 20-year offtake contracts at premium pricing is now open. It will not stay open forever.

Second, the U.S.-China conflict is creating uncertainties. The bipartisan American consensus on critical-minerals decoupling has created a Western premium for non-Chinese supply of copper, nickel, lithium, cobalt, rare earths, and graphite. British Columbia has the geology, the skilled workforce, the deep-water ports, and proximity to the world's largest user of these commodities. What BC does not yet have is a regulatory regime that can permit a mine in less than a decade. Territory-wide consent agreements with First Nations (rather than project-by-project litigation) can help solve this problem and may be single most important economic policy choice for provincial leaders to make.
Third, global demographics are shifting, and that's creating opportunities. The world's population is still growing in absolute terms, while arable land per capita is shrinking. Climate volatility is reducing yields in lower latitudes. Phosphate and potash supply chains have been disrupted by the Strait of Hormuz crisis, since the Persian Gulf moves roughly a third of global urea exports. British Columbia's agricultural land, its Saskatchewan-and-Alberta-adjacent fertilizer logistics, and its Pacific port access for grain exports give it a structural advantage in feeding a world that increasingly struggles to feed itself.

[Energy, which has usually meant oil, has been a driver of geopolitics for the past 100 years or so. As the internal combustion engine touched every aspect of life, fuel was needed for cars and trucks, industrial machines, and farm equipment. The world's militaries transitioned away from coal-fired power and grew dependent upon gasoline to power tanks, p...](https://substack.com/redirect/c724149d-126d-4d14-9d88-dd717a0588cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* * *
**These are not small opportunities. They are generational ones that share a common feature: they reward jurisdictions that can make decisions quickly, with capital that flows confidently, on firm legal foundations.**
The path forward in British Columbia must be _**growth-led reconciliation**_ , _**not** **grievance-led redistribution**_. First Nations need to convert from rights-holders-with-veto-power into co-owners-with-skin-in-the-game. The former approach risks holding projects hostage, while the latter moves forward with shared growth. BC should increase the equity-financing program and negotiate territory-wide consent frameworks. And most importantly, BC must restore investor confidence by clarifying--through legislation, not litigation--that individual property rights and collective Indigenous rights can coexist.
The thread has been pulled. The sweater is beginning to unravel. BC can either keep tugging and watch the social fabric of British Columbia unravel as capital flees and grievance compounds... or leaders can together weave something new and stronger. Instead of fighting over slices of a shrinking pie, why not grow the pie? Build an economy large enough that everyone, Indigenous and non-Indigenous, settler and newcomer, gets a bigger share than they would have fighting a zero-sum game.
The world is offering British Columbia an extraordinary opportunity. BC's leaders should be wise enough to take it.

It will not stay open forever. | | | | ---|---|--- | Jan 11 | Second, the U.S.-China conflict is creating uncertainties. The bipartisan American consensus on critical-minerals decoupling has created a Western premium for non-Chinese supply of copper, nickel, lithium, cobalt, rare earths, and graphite. British Columbia has the geology, the skilled workforce, the deep-water ports, and proximity to the world's largest user of these commodities. What BC does not yet have is a regulatory regime that can permit a mine in less than a decade. Territory-wide consent agreements with First Nations (rather than project-by-project litigation) can help solve this problem and may be single most important economic policy choice for provincial leaders to make. Third, global demographics are shifting, and that's creating opportunities. The world's population is still growing in absolute terms, while arable land per capita is shrinking. Climate volatility is reducing yields in lower latitudes. Phosphate and potash supply chains have been disrupted by the Strait of Hormuz crisis, since the Persian Gulf moves roughly a third of global urea exports. British Columbia's agricultural land, its Saskatchewan-and-Alberta-adjacent fertilizer logistics, and its Pacific port access for grain exports give it a structural advantage in feeding a world that increasingly struggles to feed itself. | | | | ---|---|--- | November 16, 2025 | These are not small opportunities. They are generational ones that share a common feature: they reward jurisdictions that can make decisions quickly, with capital that flows confidently, on firm legal foundations. The path forward in British Columbia must be growth-led reconciliation , not grievance-led redistribution. First Nations need to convert from rights-holders-with-veto-power into co-owners-with-skin-in-the-game. The former approach risks holding projects hostage, while the latter moves forward with shared growth. BC should increase the equity-financing program and negotiate territory-wide consent frameworks. And most importantly, BC must restore investor confidence by clarifying--through legislation, not litigation--that individual property rights and collective Indigenous rights can coexist. The thread has been pulled. The sweater is beginning to unravel. BC can either keep tugging and watch the social fabric of British Columbia unravel as capital flees and grievance compounds... or leaders can together weave something new and stronger. Instead of fighting over slices of a shrinking pie, why not grow the pie? Build an economy large enough that everyone, Indigenous and non-Indigenous, settler and newcomer, gets a bigger share than they would have fighting a zero-sum game. The world is offering British Columbia an extraordinary opportunity. BC's leaders should be wise enough to take it. | | ---|---|--- VIKRAM MANSHARAMANI is an entrepreneur, consultant, scholar, neighbor, husband, father, volunteer, and professional generalist who thinks in multiple-dimensions and looks beyond the short-term. Self-taught to think around corners and connect original dots, he spends his time speaking with global leaders in business, government, academia, and journalism. He 's currently the Chairman and CEO of Goodwell Foods, a manufacturer of private label frozen pizza. LinkedIn has twice listed him as its #1 Top Voice in Money & Finance, and Worth profiled him as one of the 100 Most Powerful People in Global Finance. Vikram earned a PhD From MIT, has taught at Yale and Harvard, and is the author of three books, , and **. Vikram lives in Lincoln, New Hampshire with his wife and two children, where they can usually be found hiking or skiing. body:
Dear Hoosier Republicans, No images? [Click here](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-e-akydtht-hhlljjcji-tt/) _**Putting Hoosier Families First**_ Dear Hoosier Republicans,Hoosiers are seeing real results from the work of our Republican leadership to put working families first. From expanding access to affordable child care, to helping small businesses grow with new technology, to standing up to foreign threats and cracking down on unsafe products, our party is laser-focused on making life better and more affordable for Hoosiers across the state. Our mission remains to keep Indiana strong, safe, and a place where families can get ahead.Now it's your turn to be heard. Early voting is underway, and Election Day is only two days away. Make a plan, show up, and vote, because our state's future depends on Hoosiers like you making your voice heard.As always, thank you for being a part of our team, and please feel free to reach out if there's any way I can be of assistance.Yours in service, Lana Keesling, Indiana GOP Chairwoman _**Governor Braun**_ _**Improves Child Care Access and Affordability, Supports Working Families**_ Governor Mike Braun ceremonially signed HEA 1177, expanding employer-supported child care by extending tax credit eligibility to small businesses and encouraging new local solutions. The law helps more companies offer child care options, increases access for working families, and supports the development of additional facilities across Indiana. Building on broader investments, the measure aims to ease cost pressures, strengthen the workforce, and expand opportunity for Hoosier families."Affordable child care is one of the biggest pressures on family budgets and a big challenge for Hoosier families. By expanding eligibility for Indiana's employer child care tax credit to small businesses, we expand access to reliable, affordable child care and create more options for working parents." \- Governor Braun via a [press release](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-akydtht-hhlljjcji-r/) _**Governor Braun Announces IN AI to Grow Jobs and Wages Through Human-Centered AI**_ Governor Mike Braun announced IN AI, a statewide initiative designed to help businesses adopt human-centered artificial intelligence to boost productivity, create jobs, and raise wages. Led by the Indiana Corporate Partnership, the program will connect employers with tools, talent, and technical support to apply AI in practical ways across industries. By focusing on real-world use and reaching businesses of all sizes, IN AI aims to position Indiana as a national leader in AI-driven economic growth while expanding opportunity for Hoosiers."Our goal is clear: grow wages, create more high-quality jobs, and position Indiana for long-term economic growth by making it the most AI-ready state in the nation. _IN AI _is about making sure all of our businesses - from Main Street to large organizations -- have the tools and talent they need to compete and succeed in a changing economy."\- Governor Braun via a [press release](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-akydtht-hhlljjcji-y/) _**Governor Braun Strengthens Indiana 's Competitiveness with China, Establishes Safeguards Against Foreign Adversaries**_ Governor Mike Braun signed two bills strengthening protections against foreign influence and tightening oversight of tobacco and vaping products in Indiana. The measures establish new safeguards for state contracts and institutions while giving regulators stronger tools to enforce standards and address unsafe foreign-produced products. Together, the laws aim to enhance security, protect consumers, and keep Indiana competitive in the face of global threats."We are taking action to protect Indiana from foreign adversaries trying to gain influence here at home, and from dangerous foreign-produced vaping products from entering the U.S. market. These laws make sure Indiana is competing from a position of strength and putting Hoosiers first."\- Governor Braun via a [press release](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-akydtht-hhlljjcji-j/) [](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-akydtht-hhlljjcji-t/) [Subscribe to The Braun Briefing!](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-akydtht-hhlljjcji-i/) If you want to stay up to date with everything happening in the Governor's office, don't miss out, subscribe today! _**Chairwoman's County Visits: 35**_ **Shelby County** **Hancock** **County** **Clark** **County** **Allen County** **2026 State Convention** [Click Here for More Information](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-akydtht-hhlljjcji-d/) [Confirmed Delegate Registration](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-akydtht-hhlljjcji-h/) [Delegate Fees paid by Parties/Organization](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-akydtht-hhlljjcji-k/) [Guest (Non-Delegate) Registration](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-akydtht-hhlljjcji-u/) Delegates must pay by May 12th! _**Indiana GOP is Hiring Interns for the Spring & Summer**_ **📱 _News You Can Use_ ** **Governor Mike Braun**** **[highlighted](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-akydtht-hhlljjcji-o/) his 2026 affordability agenda in stops in Ellettsville and Noblesville to meet with local leaders, discuss community priorities, and highlight efforts to ensure taxpayers are receiving the best service at the lowest cost possible, saying, "My statewide travel allows me to hear from local leaders about the issues facing their communities and to ensure state government is working with local officials to deliver the best value for taxpayers. I want to thank Mayor Chris Jensen for hosting me in Noblesville and the local officials in Ellettsville for their leadership."**Lieutenant Governor Micah Beckwith** [visited](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-akydtht-hhlljjcji-b/) with the Club America group at Westfield High School, saying, "These kids really stood out with their thoughtful and engaging questions that reflected real critical thinking. What impressed me the most wasn't just our shared agreements, but also the respectful disagreements. Even the kids who saw things differently approached our conversations with sincerity, curiosity, and good faith."**Secretary Diego Morales **[reminded](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-akydtht-hhlljjcji-n/) eligible Hoosiers to make a plan to vote on Tuesday, May 5, 2026. Secretary Morales will be traveling around the state on Primary Election Day, monitoring the election, visiting polling locations and thanking voters and poll workers. Secretary Morales plans to observe elections in several counties and cast his own vote in Marion County.**Attorney General Todd Rokita **[launched](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-akydtht-hhlljjcji-p/) IN Fuel Watch, a new public online portal that provides real-time gasoline prices at more than 4,600 Indiana gas stations around the entire state, saying, "We know every penny matters right now and are committed to making sure you are treated fairly at the pump during this time."**Treasurer Daniel Elliott **[addressed](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-akydtht-hhlljjcji-x/) the 911 directors from across the state at their annual summit, saying, "Our 911 operators are often our first responders' first responder, talking to people at their worst possible moment. It was important for me to express my gratitude and thanks to our heroes."**Comptroller Elise Nieshalla **[celebrated](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-akydtht-hhlljjcji-m/) Governor Braun ceremonially signing _SEA 14_ , authorizing an increase to the employer match for Indiana's Deferred Compensation Retirement Plan, Hoosier START, saying, "When we identified that the match amount was still at $15, the original amount when the benefit started 26 years ago, we got to work finding a budget-neutral way to bring it in line with present-day value, which helps the State maintain a competitive retirement package for employees."**Senator Todd Young**[co-introduced](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-akydtht-hhlljjcji-c/)** ** the _Workforce Apprenticeship Growth and Education Support (WAGES) Act_. The legislation would create a refundable payroll tax credit for employers who maintain or participate in a Registered Apprenticeship Program (RAP). The tax credit would offset the cost of wages paid to apprentices and mentors, as well as the cost of other program expenses. **Senator Jim Banks**[introduced](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-akydtht-hhlljjcji-q/) the _Promoting Access and Revenue Integrity Through Institutional Transparency (PARITY) Act_. This bill would repeal the 90/10 rule in the _Higher Education Act_ , which only applies to proprietary schools and requires them to derive at least 10 percent of their revenue from non-federal sources, saying, "Right now, the rules single out vocational and career schools while letting other colleges play by a different set of standards. That's not fair when these programs are helping meet critical workforce needs and keeping our economy moving."**Congressman Rudy Yakym**[celebrated](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-akydtht-hhlljjcji-a/) the House Ways and Means Committee unanimously passing the _Support for Expectant and Parenting Foster Youth Act_ , the bipartisan legislation authored by Congressman Rudy Yakymand Ranking Member Danny K. Davis to the House Floor. The bill strengthens coordination between the Maternal, Infant, and Early Childhood Home Visiting (MIECHV) and Chafee programs to better serve foster youth who are expecting or raising children of their own.**Congressman Marlin Stutzman **[met](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-akydtht-hhlljjcji-f/) with the American Association of Nurse Anesthesiology to discuss increasing their services among rural communities, saying, "I admire their hard work and dedication to providing top care to Hoosiers in need!"**Congressman Jim Baird **[voted](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-akydtht-hhlljjcji-z/) in favor of S. Con. ## Project Freedom Begins in Hormuz Today
The U.S. Navy [begins escorting](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHOozAQBOCnMZ2R2RgMhYtr6HLtlWiN12FPBiPbCco9_Sl5hb8eaTTf_Lkvd-TIx-M37mRrSMtBV4lUK-Wl5ud-uoyHJ-8wO6ZScT8LLqBgkKqXSi8eOb4X3XgbiIBuDdnOGDOOUzdMzWbNQGbsjVK9D75zRgMEnGDVk8c1qKlh-2lTvdKdUoMy7ahHWgci524QjAahFXmuKbd_Ex91oxDf6UW5XdPeRLvVehZx-yVgFjBf19WurnwUn1zAHPlF8nl6rFQEzJzxkBdm-dXJUjNylSnILeX9-U9yyUhRRnJ4pEOuhIUCZxIwN9n68-IYuQxGaPXYkeN3Rf3RdS8L_wMAAP__zJaFeA) commercial ships out of the Strait of Hormuz today under "Project Freedom," an effort to free neutral vessels that have been stuck since Iran closed the waterway. Trump announced the move Sunday on Truth Social, calling it a "humanitarian gesture" for ships low on food, and warning any interference "will be dealt with forcefully." [Read the post here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2K6zAUBOCnsbqEI1l_LlRcuLjLVgtbmmPpONYiW0ZSEvL2i_cVtp2BD2a-btMNY4r7_QM3cm3J006vmqg1KlMrj-2YC-6BwoxljlQbbkfFSYDQF1AXkFPAmN6TZMEtRIJ6Ro4bY6wduB7Y6vyg0fpFolUqCPTWWB4WDiC96cHMLLpTAwWSA2gwVysteU00z71YjBSdBAqx5XL9znFvKy3pnZ9Urj5vLLm1taN2_b9OjJ0YW3m0tWYfMZ39GUoohOl_3jGFz3NSJ8Yj11Y7MXKuFRdKKS56ZQdugBUXjldMKVZtOgn3DeMvxdqf_nk68RMAAP__hjF3jg). Hours earlier, a bulk carrier [reported being attacked](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkb2OnTAQhZ8GurkyxthQUKSh27QpkX-GZXINRsPcRTdPH7HKG6Q6xXd0pE_n18f84SnT_vnTbzjKUuYdrzOjCPIs_NqOwH5PmILnQHiK347Tz1ppC6oDZebkKb9nU6dxQdTY1jg2zrm-Hxo71OvYtcYmm9A11rtGL4s1rnWmw6UbnOr7msZ7TXXKNEpZ5R696TFaxBBavTijK6MwkRR-_C60y4pLfpcv5EcsW53HVeQ4q_ZHpadKT9d1PWI4-xtWevIsFDNWerq97vBCZYercE43F_HxCWUHYr9Xegqv_ITomQkZ_tFT2JNAWWAtvL3-fHfh8gyv5yYFApPQucJGmcTzG2iPlHAXYDwKS6WnTjmIoXWxCxpS61sw1vcQYujABhsTtkMYgqp5TMdFOdNpXWXU5-Ypf4vKf73zNeq_AQAA__-UAaUV) by small craft off Sirik, Iran, the 24th such incident since the war began. All crew were safe. Trump is also weighing a 14-point [Iranian peace proposal](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGOrDAQRE9jMlDTGBsCBz8hm59uiNqmGbwy2DLeQXP7FXOFTSop6ZXqfT3mB_ngj-d_2tmUNc4HX2fgUjjPJf_syWY6Fl4sZev5LLSnk2YEVDX0Nch5IR_es6wWszIjdxWbVms9DGOrxmozklAi9S13vXJsSVnU4zoohtVB37WVNzcNepAtgALdDHJgp5it7XDVEoUEXnyJufmO_igbr-EdX5wbF_cqmK2UdIrun8BJ4HRdV-MO6-5S4HSjBU7Q39EJnD6fap_pqC_KdWJyXKccUzwpNFvZQ5XNki4fgj-VFhKeO_nw2Sp_EvQy-BsAAP__9xl45w) calling for the strait to reopen within 30 days, though he wrote Tehran hasn't "paid a big enough price."
## Trump's Name on Buildings, Currency
The Trump administration has added the president's name or image to [more than a dozen](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2upSAURp8GO04QUbSgmMbuTjul2bC3Hib8GOBcc95-4plHuPVKVr71_fnavsAHn47fEMm0PW-JrhqoNSpbK6942gIJCS0U66k2iGeFTQo5cTFyoTYEH96b6tDsRJKGjkyvtZ7npZ-W7mlAD5PWKJV2C1qwy97jNErcR4VKWdF5c9vEKFQvxCT0Y1YzuYnI2kHuWkmmBKFvuTz-Zp_ak_bwzt9UHi7HLphna2dlwy8mVybX67oeybq74uZMrmcOvnlXmVwxJwjIP11MrjshFQj8uG0pUmocEOt_zhNE4j7CQdy-fECfjsrPko8CsXL3KoWSe_PiEgxqEIvuisHz8iH4OmmmxBHBh8_I9qNnv438FwAA__8G5pD5) federal buildings, programs, and U.S. currency since the beginning of his second term. In December, the [Donald J. Trump U.S. Institute of Peace](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFywyAQheHToM6eZYUWVFCkUee0KTUgVjYZJDSA7fj2GecK6d684iv-r8t8cTHF_frpNrZtzfPOz5q4NS5zK_ft8MXtgYN3xUeuzW1HdTMC0gmGE6g5uJhes-qCXZmR-46t1FobM0oau5v1Qx80aSTo0XuJy2gGCJIceO1Aqy7atwYDKAlAoM9GGV6I2fseV61QKOAQWy7n7xz3duM1vfKDy3nJW5fsrbWjiv5D4CRw-nm_AqfKS7n7mN-zuXavAic5jtSTQZIGNRFJUF2x4XjGlGIlLRRcNxfTH9z-VeNh8TcAAP__VvBwKg) became the first federal building named for a sitting U.S. president, followed by the renamed Donald J. Trump and John F. Kennedy Memorial Center for the Performing Arts. The Treasury also plans to add Trump's signature to future paper currency, alongside a commemorative [24-carat gold coin](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOnDAURb_GdEbmYWwoXIwi0USkSCKlRAY_My-ygbW9g-bvVzO_sN3VLa7uOf-mebIUaN9-2Yim-GPe8coBS8E0l_QZzyXZ3aFbbFoIc7HxzHYGAYqLjgs5O0vhOcvKGY8I2FZoGq113w-NGqq70VI13nUCrZZyEbpvnWrA2qHpYPUdVmRea6ITshFCCV33ssdVIS5LC15LYFKgo3Kk-v9Be7mjD8_jgalej1gFcy_lzKy9MRgZjNd11au39XY8GIz5mQtGBqOngJnBGBEL7RuPtmAiG15dz3-MN94M0-03KK75RHvhb8I_GOmDg_zJoAPx96XjndaDdn4mzPXpfJWMOy8KgbLSTIotWgrvb-VbQh8GvgIAAP__KlqHTw) and a $1 coin tied to America's 250th anniversary. Other branding includes Trump-class battleships, the $1 million Trump gold card, [limited-edition passports](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL_uozAQhJ8GOkdmMYYULq5J97v2SrTGS_DJ_2RvgvL2J_IKV3-j0Xzz52f9QR98ev7GSIb3vCY6WyBmqivXVyy2YnLkLFbrqTHG0nAFCVrISUi1OvThs6remZ0IaOzJDPM8L8t90Pf-MBaGaZv0uCPcrZ0WxMWqYdQDbBrA7b03V5ucpBqk1HK-LWqhTRNZO8I-K-iUJOc519vf7BMftIdPflO9bTn2wRzMpXXjrw4eHTzO87wlu10WF-_gUXLw7LfWwcPlhMGJr9dFKjXvKLHwEZ8kXk0UbK3kyk20V4xURWNkEo4KVo5XFCbJh8CU_Jtqw_oRdUs4Kpj03FfjyulD8E3PnZLPiD58Z_J_ffs28C8AAP__0YCRSQ) featuring his image, Trump Accounts for children, and government websites TrumpIRA.gov and TrumpRx.gov.
## Barbie Stamps Coming This Summer
The U.S. Postal Service unveiled 10 new commemorative Barbie stamps, featuring Mattel's iconic doll in career roles ranging from astronaut and surgeon to paleontologist and music star. [See the Barbie stamps here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOozAQhJ_GdEaLYxtSuLiGLtdeidZ4CT4ZjOxNUN7-xOUR_m6kkWbmmz-P6YExxf35GzdyvORpp7MmYqYycXlthy-4Bwoei49UGbej4qRAWQlGgp4CxvSZdBPcQqTo1pDr-r4fhntn783qjLkvnZ0H03vAeZg1Kgug1DJbYwKFJrorDQzoDsBC3w56oNkSeX9TS6-V0EAhci7t3xx3XmlJn_ym0s55a5JbmY8qbr-EGoUa0ecXt6961MsWarx4Sv5K5Jh3TLJQIqxUhRqvbqFGMNDJL6PkLD3JmRL5gkxBnpFXudMpv_jtyltTXDjOmFKsthcanhvG9H8Q_-jFt1P_AgAA__9lx4di). The stamps will officially [debut July 11](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOozAQBuCnMZ2jYQwYChcnnbjmsu2WyOCBzMo2yHYS5e1XbB5h2xnp1__9n9fpatlz3D5sIFPWfYr0zJ5KoTSVdA_HnGx05GabZqZcbDiynRCwk9BKaCZn2b-mpnJmJUJSFZlaa933Q90N1c1Ab91KCmrVD2RJDdSvQ4cIi11A123F5kyDFpoaoAN96Zuelo5onhWuukHRADkue7p87RzLjVb_2h-ULsseKm9upRxZqD8CR4GjnZdTcP4Ejv-u5_k_PzhuAsd7PrJM5MlmjpusQUZ6yjdNvm0y30OgJHDMZU8voUZ2Qv2tFbadHkBXybjjyd5z7rRoYAuW_U-T8qv5Hga_AwAA__8FwYMa) at the 2026 National Barbie Doll Collectors Convention in Austin, Texas. USPS art director Ethel Kessler designed the set with Mattel, [leaning into "Barbie Pink"](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO3CAQBuCnwR2r8RiDXbhI4-7SprQGGN8SgXGAW-vePvLmEVJNMdKv__t_fWwfFGI4Pn9S4qXteTv4qpFb47K18pVOW-jw7C0VG7g2SmelDQG1hFGC2jyF-L2pzi87M_LQ8dIbY6Zp7vXcPRdmmNQMgyVtvMNdK9_PoEalfD8OburCcqfBCKoH0GAek5rYaWZrB9yNQqGAfWi5PH7ncLQn7_E7v7g8XE5dXJ6tnVUMPwSuAtfruh7XH_L3U-BKpQUXWeB6u-5DLeRDXrlEL3D9qvLMtVGUlcsrOJb_oNLllDjlQi28WL7dsnITuI5gJA7ODBYmqb13Ulmt5EwjS69mQJz9QLh3ZfHnFWIMVRuh4DNRiO_O7b-Gfi34NwAA__-ftpEG) and a rare format, a third taller than typical vertical commemorative stamps. Introduced in 1959, Barbie has [represented more than 250 careers](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L3uozAQBPCnMR1oWRwMhYtr6HLtlWjBC_jkL9lOorz9KZdH-Pej0fzmz329k3U2nL_Js65HXAO_iuNaOa81P3zaMgXDZqO8WS6VfCq0IuDYwq0FuRqy7r3KxuiDGXloWPdKqWma-3FuLg1EKPmYod9hHNUMitU8qV0RTmQmaKz-tMENZA8wguomOfE-Mm_bgIeSKCSwsTXm7m-0oV58uHd8cu726Bunr1pTEcMvgYvApVwxJRvO7k1XjJ-IwOXkwJmcwIVytbvjInB5lFTazI6p2HC2X2D7Fbbl4T3nFlEiDgqwu6p3TdYmvaxztoxKSDg9Wfd_Rf3RdU-N_wIAAP__zd2Dog) over six decades and remains the best-selling doll of all time. The new Forever stamps will retail at first-class postage rates.

I grew up on Star Trek: The Next Generation. I still remember being introduced to it in 1987 when Encounter at Farpoint first aired. My **Unc** was a Star Trek fan from the original series, and he told me there was a new Star Trek coming out and that I needed to watch it. I did, and I was immediately hooked.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8d2ba138-62f4-4289-91aa-5c09b06c76f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Captain Jean-Luc "The GOAT" Picard
I recorded every episode on VHS. I would sit there stopping and starting the tape so I could cut out the commercials, and I honestly do not think I missed more than a couple episodes during the entire run of the series. My dad kept those tapes for a long time, until my late 30's, until eventually we realized you could just buy the whole series on DVD, download it, or stream it like a normal person. But that process, looking back, was part of the obsession. It was part of the ritual. It was part of loving something before everything was available instantly.
Star Trek is deep in my heart. A lot of people may not know this about me, but I am a big nerd. Science, philosophy, sci-fi, all of it. I did not just watch Star Trek. One of my favorite classes in college was Philosophy and Star Trek, taught by Dr. Kathy Ferguson, who later became my thesis mentor. I wanted to write about Kantian philosophy in Star Trek. Her class was brilliant because she took Hegel, Mill, Kant, and so many others, then showed how those ideas played out inside Star Trek episodes.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f33c65df-20f7-4d22-8f1d-976d7e9c2a80?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Dr. Ferguson
So when I came across this picture of the ten best Captain Picard quotes from The Next Generation, I kept thinking about it. Not because this is some deep academic breakdown, but because these quotes really did impact me and thousands others. They shaped my personality, my goals, my morals, my ideology, and the way I think about leadership, politics, truth, compromise, failure, and power.
Picard had this code. No compromise, but also enough judgment to know when the rule itself had to be questioned. He believed in sacrifice over self-indulgence. He carried this stoicism that was not always healthy, and in many ways, Picard was a sad lonely man. But for some reason, I admired that too. Maybe because he showed that leadership is not about being happy all the time. Sometimes it is about carrying the weight and still doing the right thing.
**Here are 10 great Captain Picard Quotes and what they mean to me.**
* * *
### 10\. "Let's see what's out there. Engage."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/26cb7628-b97a-4151-bbfe-97f971f9d572?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I am a creature of habit. I love comfort. There is nothing better than sleeping in my own bed, taking a shower in my own bathroom, and living inside the small rituals that make life feel stable. I have never been the traveling hippie type. I know people who can go anywhere, sleep anywhere, camp anywhere, move from place to place, and feel perfectly fine. I know people from the military who can do that without thinking twice. That is not me.
But at the same time, I cannot stay in one place forever. There is too much out there. I need to explore. That is why I moved to Hawaii. That is why I moved to China. That is why I lived in Taiwan. That is why I have been to more than 40 countries and learned foreign languages, because every culture and every language adds another layer to how you understand the world. The more time you spend outside your own bubble, the more depth you get.
And to be perfectly honest, that can be a lonely place. Not everybody has those experiences, and not everybody understands what it does to you. But trust me, the people who do understand find each other.
* * *
### 9\. "There can be no justice so long as laws are absolute. Even life itself is an exercise in exceptions."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ef5607f7-fab9-48a7-8d97-ec40474cf081?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I do not even remember the episode this quote came from, but as soon as I read it again, I thought, yeah, this is rebel Matt.
I do not believe laws are absolute. I never have. I am the guy who sees a no right turn on red sign and, if it is clear and nobody is being hurt, I am probably taking the turn. That may sound small, but that is the point. There are rules we follow because they protect people, and there are rules we follow because somebody wrote them down and nobody has questioned them since.
This one hit me because of recent Supreme Court rulings. Laws should be examined. Laws should be challenged. Laws should be changed. And yes, sometimes existing laws need to be broken, because shit, sometimes we have evolved. Sometimes a law was right for one moment, one context, one version of society, and then it becomes the opposite of what we wanted to achieve.
It means justice means change and change means there are no absolutes.
* * *
### 8\. "There are times, sir, when men of good conscience cannot blindly follow orders."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c24e5ed4-1f7b-46c4-ba1e-459b12bb67c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Senator Mark Kelly
This one immediately made me think of Senator Mark Kelly and his statement about troops following orders under President Trump. There are two sides to this, and both are very valid. On one hand, you cannot have a military where everyone just disobeys orders because they personally do not like them. That creates chaos, and there have to be consequences for that.
But at the same time, you cannot have troops blindly following orders if those orders turn them into tools of something immoral, homicidal, genocidal, or unlawful. I am not saying that is what Trump is doing. I **AM** saying there has to be a line.
And this does not only apply to the military. It applies to your boss. It applies to your political party. It applies to your friends. It applies to yourself. At some point, you have to be able to say, no, I am not doing that. The more clearly you draw that line before the moment comes, the more likely you are to actually hold it when it matters. No matter the consequences.
* * *
### 7\. "Let's make sure history never forgets the name... Enterprise."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/19e54b33-cf86-42c6-96b8-d120b431edc8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
NCC 1701 D
Here lies my ego.
I do not know why I am on this earth, and I do not think most people really know either. But I know this. I do not want to die and be forgotten. I do not want to have no impact. I do not want to live a life, fade away, and have nobody remember me two generations from now.
If we are not trying to do something big, then what the hell are we doing? Go big or go home. I know that is not for everybody, and yes, I probably judge people for it more than I should. But I believe we are supposed to ruffle feathers. We are supposed to make waves in still water. I do not want to leave this earth without contributing something positive, something real, something that mattered.
* * *
### 6\. "You cannot explain away a wantonly immoral act because you think that it is connected to some higher purpose."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/75b17671-7b69-4eaa-8583-40a46cb34569?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This one is very relevant because of what we see in politics all the time. Money starts flowing, outside groups start spending on behalf of a candidate, and suddenly everyone wants to pretend the principle changes depending on who benefits. I want to be very clear because people love to twist shit. This is not about one specific candidate. This is about the system. It is about whether we actually believe money in politics is corrupting, or whether we only believe that when the money is helping someone we do not like.
When people say, "Well, you need money to run a race," they are not wrong. You do. But that does not erase the principle. You can still say you are against corporate money in politics. You can still say Super PACs are corrosive. You can still say the system is fucked, even if the system helps someone you like.
You do not get to explain away an immoral act because you think it is connected to some higher purpose, like winning office. Maybe you think your side deserves the exception. Maybe you think the ends justify the means. But does that make it right?
* * *
### 5\. "The first duty of every Starfleet officer is to the truth, whether it's scientific truth or historical truth or personal truth. It's the guiding principle on which Starfleet is based."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/19fe3cf8-f6cd-4a7c-bd8c-e59c60b7e4c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Star Fleet Academy, San Francisco
When I ran for office in 2022, I dealt with personal truth quite a bit. In 2024, I broke out of the consultant-driven version of campaigning and tried to run a campaign that was actually mine. My ideas. My instincts. My voice. My purpose.
Now I feel like I am on a different mission, which is trying to find truth in a broader sense. What do we actually want out of the United States? What do we want out of democracy? How much truth do people really want?
But truth is not just one thing. There is scientific truth, historical truth, political truth, and personal truth. The guiding principle should be figuring out what truth you are actually operating from. If you do not know that, then you are just reacting. You are not thinking. You are not leading. You are just being pushed around by whatever pressure hits you next.
* * *
### 4\. "With the first link, the chain is forged. The first speech censored, the first thought forbidden, the first freedom denied, chains us all irrevocably."
[](https://substack.com/redirect/c7814ed3-8491-4aab-b7c2-59af8a4ac48d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This might be my favorite quote in all of Star Trek. It may be tied with another one, but this one is personal. This is not just about politics. This is about who you are and the decisions we make and what we allow.
I think about this every time someone in politics says, well, it is just a little compromise. Just take the money. Just look the other way. Just soften the statement. Just make the deal. Just vote for this one thing. Just go along this one time.
But with the first link, the chain is forged.
People do not think one small compromise changes how they legislate, how they represent people, or how they can be manipulated in the future. But it does. That first link matters because once it is attached to you, somebody can pull it. And once somebody can pull it, you are not as free as you were before.
I also think about this with our data, our privacy, AI, online manipulation, corporate control, and every app being designed like a slot machine. We keep acting like the first step does not matter. But it does.
It is like addiction. The danger is not just thinking about heroin. The danger is the first time you do it. That is when the path starts.
So how much compromise do you take? How much do you endure? How many times do you look the other way before you realize the chain is already around your neck?
* * *
### 3\. "It is possible to commit no mistakes and still lose. That is not a weakness; that is life."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/65f4a953-ba36-4b86-bdaa-2dedcc297e83?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This is tied for my favorite Picard quote because I think about it all the time. I think about it for myself, but I also think about it for other people. I know people who started businesses and failed. I know people who started businesses, succeeded, and then failed later. I know people who did everything they were supposed to do and still ended up struggling.
And the truth is, some people do reckless things. Some people gamble, cheat, lie, or self-destruct. But most of the people I know who failed were not those people. They were people who tried hard, made decisions, worked their asses off, and still lost. The decisions did not work out, but that does not mean the decisions were stupid. It means life is brutal sometimes.
That is why I believe in a social safety net. Not because everyone who struggles is inadequate. But, sometimes people just lose. And when they do, a decent society does not treat them like garbage for it.
* * *
### 2\. "There. Are. Four. Lights."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4f5cdc4c-5dc5-426f-a735-22eb3e788ff7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This is the power quote of power quotes.
If you do not know Star Trek, it may not make sense. But Captain Jean-Luc Picard was captured by the Cardassians, and they tried to break him. They wanted him to say there were five lights when there were only four. It was not really about the lights. It was about breaking his mind, his hope, his spirit, and his ability to trust what he knew was true.
And he did not break.
He said, "There! Are! Four! Lights!"
That means he refused to capitulate. He refused to give in to torture. He refused to say something false just to stop the pain. I honestly think everyone should watch that episode at least once a year, just to remember that whatever you are going through, however hard it gets, do not break.
But I also think this quote hits differently now because of what we consume every day. It is not just about torture in some distant sci-fi prison cell. It is about what people tell us is true, what media tells us is true, what algorithms push in front of us, and what we know in our gut is wrong.
We live in a time where manipulation is everywhere. Some of it comes from inside our own country. Some of it comes from outside of it. Now we have deepfakes, AI-generated bullshit, edited videos, fake screenshots, propaganda farms, and endless online narratives all trying to make people doubt what they saw, what they know, and what they believe.
That is what makes this lesson so important. People can look at the same video, the same event, the same set of facts, and walk away with completely different interpretations. Some of that is human nature, but some of it is intentional. The goal is to wear you down. The goal is to make you so confused, so tired, and so overwhelmed that you eventually give in and say whatever version of reality makes the pressure stop.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/e8999775-f859-4866-94ac-7d069796ef97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
And that is where the strength comes in. Being grounded in truth, whether that is factual truth, personal truth, or moral truth, is not always popular. It is not always comfortable. Sometimes the easier path is to capitulate. Sometimes the more rewarding path, financially, socially, or politically, is to just say '**there are five lights '** and move on with your life.
But that is the whole point. The strength is seeing the situation clearly, knowing what is true, and refusing to let manipulation pull you away from it. It is not stubbornness for the sake of stubbornness. It is the discipline to say, no, I know what I saw. I know what happened. I know what is true.
**There! Are! Four! Lights!**
* * *
### 1\. "Seize the time, Meribor. Live now. Make now always the most precious time. Now will never come again."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7dff3f66-dcf6-4d0d-98bf-428da127e604?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This is probably the most Buddhist thing you could ever hear from Star Trek. Everybody talks about living in the now, but most people do not do it. We live in the future. We live in the past. We predict. We project. We worry. We replay old mistakes. We make decisions today based on imaginary futures that may never happen.
But the truth is, we do not know. We do not know what is coming. We do not know how long we have. We do not know which moment is going to matter until it is gone.
So why not make now the time? Why not live in the now and let it move over you like waves? Do not try to control every second of it. Do not plan so obsessively that you forget to actually experience your life. I think a lot of people would be happier if they stopped trying to manage every possible future and started being present in the one moment they actually have.
* * *
That is what these quotes mean to me. Some political. Some personal. Some probably obvious. Some maybe not that deep. But they are mine. Star Trek shaped me. Picard shaped me. Philosophy shaped me. And whether I am talking about campaigns, corruption, truth, law, compromise, or just trying not to break, I can still hear these lines in the back of my head.
That is what old Star Trek gives you. It gives you a moral question without handing you a clean answer,. That was the beauty of it. It was never on the nose. It was not just an action show. It was not empty entertainment in space uniforms. It was asking real questions about society, power, identity, duty, faith, work, love, marriage, race, gender, sexuality, and what it actually means to be decent when there is no perfect choice in front of you. Or how doing the right thing might actually make you a villain.
That is why I always encourage people to go back and watch the old episodes. Star Trek would put these questions in front of you, let the characters wrestle with them, and then refuse to insult you by pretending there was always one obvious answer. The crew still had to act. Picard still had to make a decision.
And that is the part I miss. That image of Picard staring out the window of his ready room, quietly carrying the choice he just made, is more powerful than most shows yelling their entire moral argument at you from some superiority high horse. It leaves you wondering whether he made the right call, or whether there was ever a right call to begin with.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b3d0df4b-9a1e-43e0-9289-796453dc174f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
That was the beauty of Star Trek. It forced you to wrestle with ethical questions without treating you like a child. It was humbling. It reminded us that you can think hard, act in good faith, do everything right, and still lose.
That is not weakness. That is life.
