Friend,

This National Teacher Appreciation Week, I’m honored to announce that the National Educators Association has officially endorsed our campaign!

https://secure.actblue.com/donate/SEMD-03-Email-2026-FR-q2?&refcode=E29466-20260504-EndorsementNEA-Image-EndorsementOrg&amount=30 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/SEMD-03-Email-2026-FR-q2?&refcode=E29466-20260504-EndorsementNEA-Image-EndorsementOrg&amount=30]

It’s safe to say that I wouldn’t be in Congress without the support of our educators from my first election in 2018 to today. This recognition means so much to me; it’s an acknowledgment of our shared belief that public education is the foundation of a thriving community. I’m a very proud product of public schools. My parents were both civil servants who taught me that supporting teachers is the “rising tide”— when we invest in our educators, everyone else rises too. They are the cornerstone of our work to build a better future for Maryland — the mentors, counselors, and steady hand guiding our children to success.

My job in Congress is to ensure we're showing up for our educators with the same level of dedication. That means focusing on:

🧒 Investing in Early Childhood Success: Expanding access to affordable child care so that our students all start on a level playing field.

🧑🏫 Supporting our Educators: Ensuring our educators can actually afford to live and raise their own families in the communities where they teach.

💵 Securing Vital Resources: Working closely with educators and families to bring more federal funds to Maryland's classrooms, including funding for special education.

I’m proud to have the NEA standing alongside me as we work to make our schools a place where every student can succeed, and every educator feels valued. I can’t wait to see what we can all achieve for the educators and students of the Third District.

Our educators show up for our children every single day — now it’s our turn to show up for them. Chip in what you can now to help keep me in Congress, working to deliver the resources they need to succeed >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/SEMD-03-Email-2026-FR-q2?&refcode=E29466-20260504-EndorsementNEA-SL-EndorsementOrg&amount=30]

Thank you,

Sarah Elfreth

Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth broke barriers in 2024, becoming the youngest woman ever elected to Congress from Maryland. She went to Congress with one thing in mind: delivering for Maryland families on the issues that matter most. Whether it's standing up for federal workers, supporting veterans, protecting the Chesapeake Bay, or tackling the affordability crisis head-on, Sarah is on the front lines, fighting for what is right. And Sarah has delivered on her promises. She has spent her first year in the House advocating for the Third District, successfully passing five bills into law, solving over 1,000 constituent cases, and bringing tens of millions in funding back to her community. She learned her work ethic and tenacity from growing up in a union household and honed her skills of problem-solving and collaborating over six years in the Maryland State Senate. Sarah lives in Annapolis with her fiancé, Eric, and their dog, Ollie. body:
We need to put partisan politics aside to help the people of Ohio.

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130747972/618787051/76101138?amount=10&refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.05.04_Amy-Acton_B1_F1_S1_C1_90OP-NC_RS-T0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODg1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2MjgzZDgwOS0wYjQ4LWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=FwvGUPAZjauMOoBs-NfICffpgZROrNwxgnbg_-hooeQ=) I’m Dr. Amy Acton, and I’m the Democratic candidate for governor of Ohio.

I grew up in Youngstown, Ohio, struggling through abuse, neglect, and hunger — and even spent one winter living in a tent.

I often share that public schools saved my life. After pulling myself out of poverty, I worked three jobs to put myself through med school.

Throughout my career, I’ve always worked with both sides of the aisle — because I’ll work with anyone who wants to solve problems instead of making them. In 2019, I was appointed by a Republican governor to lead the Ohio Department of Health. I held drug companies accountable, kept communities healthy, and was called to serve during the most unprecedented public health crisis of our lifetimes.

I’m a doctor, not a politician, but I am a public servant.

**I’m running for governor because people in my state are struggling, and I refuse to look the other way while bad actors and special interests keep taking Ohio backwards on nearly every measure.**

The problems we face don’t care if you’re a Democrat or a Republican. They’re just problems that need to be fixed. And I don’t care if you’re a Democrat or a Republican, either. I’ll fight for you and your family just the same.

_But I can’t win this race alone; that’s why I’m asking for your help today._

We’re up against a Trump-endorsed, MAGA billionaire backed by other out-of-state billionaires. My opponent, Vivek Ramaswamy, just dropped **$10 MILLION** in this race to try and defeat me because he knows Ohioans aren’t falling for the MAGA playbook.

Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime.

Now, Coach Tuberville is running for Governor so he can continue representing Alabamians and Americans in his homestate of Alabama. The Radical Left thinks they can flip Alabama blue and turn it into the California of the South. Can he count on your support? _

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson. In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others. In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime. Now, Coach Tuberville is running for Governor so he can continue representing Alabamians and Americans in his homestate of Alabama. The Radical Left thinks they can flip Alabama blue and turn it into the California of the South. Can he count on your support? |

|

Sponsored By:
[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0LFu6yAUxvGnwVssOOCDMzBc3chbolSp1NHCcJKgYmMBjl-_Sh-h8_fpN_y_zuPZhhiWx8XOZHK9jz75sWxrpplc2nIt9kXFTinXkJYROOCBdweuxiWOovHGO2-Fa8gIrfVRohLQPA32CJ1FhEn7o9YSLO-0VrzveoAOdRPMm-IdVyCFlNAiIk3C90Tee06KKW4j5dpmWrcpBmeXasv3PWVHrUtzE82z1rUw-Y_BwGDY9719bAdyaX7vDAY4qSv2xxuDQYL6uNzeNyaHsk2CydPn9X-TjV_3EGMoqJnij9mG-KvXP8R4GfgJAAD___a1aoM)
The Permanent Campaign is brought to you today in partnership with
Republican Task Force Issue: 5/4/2026
SCOTUS Pauses Mifepristone Mail Ban

[Justice Samuel Alito](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckD2OwyAQhU9jd0T8GdsFxTbpsu2WFjDjZLTYIMDJ9VeOcoLtZvSkp-97P7fl5ijSfv92G9rS1gUSLPXIBTcM6SituidW51NplPZFcmkYHxjXyx4X0YOFAE6EHq0Yx3FWRgvZP-zkg54nrz2CmLwcFPfzMJvAV67E7FRP9qziA9dSCaXkxRiDXsCECAAcdae5i1japWA-fKTg9ubq75pKwEtIWx_to7VcO_XVyWsnry7v-KpndD6lUYh4Xh90linGyjZaMReqLe3IPp7sLcpiOqiS2x3jg1I4KTCj0NMKK4ZBeQEcFA8CJ9cXC_lFMVI1Y6f5fXMU31DtHxs-rfwLAAD__8YXgnM) on Monday temporarily blocked a 5th Circuit ruling that banned telehealth prescriptions and the mailing of the abortion pill Mifepristone. The administrative stay runs until at least May 11 at 5 p.m. ET, giving drugmakers time to appeal. The New Orleans-based 5th Circuit issued its order Friday, threatening to upend access in states where abortion remains legal. Danco Laboratories and GenBioPro filed an [emergency appeal](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckD2O5CAQRk-DM1pQxtgdEGzirDfd0OKnaKMtGwtwz_VH7pm5wMQlvfre-_dYHjZR2p9_7YamtLiEHJZ6HgU39PksrdoXVutyaSnvCwjQXAxcqGWnRXbBBB-s9B0aOY7jvddKQrcaLachBqdjPyicHN4jOClV9L0XKKXukrlQYhAKetn3cNNao5NhQgwhCFRMCUtY2q3gcTpK3u7N1v8xF483n7eOzNraUVn_h8HMYG4rronoujGYCz5PstdmBvNbhDvbGmFlMA-TBnlXfEsRj5JqyzvyH0d-JCJezqsK_y7BvwiWUssM5q6YcHwkolT1yJR4bja9H3ftFw1fBj4DAAD__3KjhDE) to the Supreme Court on Saturday seeking a pause. The fight over mail access to Mifepristone returns to the full court after the stay expires. The order lands six months before the [November midterms](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckD1uxCAUhE-DO1vwjMEuKNK427QpLQzPuyj8Cdj19SOvkgukmWakb_TN1227aeddvH_qgKq0Y7PJbvWZCwY06Vla1S-sek-luRQ3oCB6OvWUb9FvrLPKGquZ6VAxKeUyCs6ge6h5meU8oQGUhxCcLXxezCGXCTg_pnnvnLpQdKIcRjaOMAghcGd2RrTWUuSEU-2xtKFgfu7eGR2brt9HKgYHk0Ln1aO1XMn4QWAlsJ7nOZi4m6sksF54AiudruAE1l-p_m3V_xn12XnfB3dgLq62FHF4tOC7omw-nfeuCkk4vQft_Hu2_eOll4KfAAAA___Gx3cD), reinserting abortion as a live political issue. Louisiana has until May 11 to respond. ★★★
U.S. Denies Iran Warship Strike

Iran's state media claimed Monday that Iranian forces struck a U.S. warship in the Strait of Hormuz with two missiles, forcing it to retreat. [U.S. Central Command](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0DFuxCAUBNDT4A4LMIt3C4o07jZtSuvDx2sUMNYHr6WcPnKOkGaakd5I8_WcnxBT3F6fkIOltsxYcK7HTiEHXw5qFd6hgivUYtlmJZTh4saFnrc0yw4tegTpu2DlOI6PwWiputVqROMXJ0dAJ4ZgjNBaS4RFuMe43H0X7UWJm9BqkMOgemNMcBLvISCiCJppASlQ6ynsh0vRw9agfi-FfOh9yV2ya2t7ZcMHUxNT03mevd-cv0qmpotnahK3KzRTUyTY-AnEGx1557URxMbLwtdC-fjp15ZTRxb3M6YUqxmZFq8MMf2ttX-c87bqNwAA__9z0nQx) flatly denied the claim, saying two American-flagged ships successfully transited the Strait without incident. The confrontation follows Trump's Sunday announcement of ["Project Freedom,"](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL3OozAURJ_GdEbGGJsULrahy7ZbohvfS_Cuwcg_QcnTr8gjfO3oaGZ0_tznO_jg9-dv2MimsswYcc71SLSRizWVDC_K8Iip-LjPUkjNxcCFmvcwdw1adAida8h2xphbr1Unm9UaDUaoETsgCaMwg-oN6sHdHI7jiLfG26tKDELJvut72Wqt6dHhSISIghRTAgKl0iY66iN4B3uB_G-JyVHr4tYEu5ZyZNb_YnJicjrPs4XwFz5ECS6CyWmnMzM5XVNMTgOTk2Jy8gl2fkLaM6-Zl8hzgTePtfC48DWmrX44LIUSL6luB8_w_pKnD4E_q0fiefVHbpLF4wp91oYp8dzAh--38gOVLyv_BwAA__-U8oT4) an operation to escort oil tankers stranded in the Strait amid the ongoing U.S.-Israel war on Iran. Tehran warned the mission violates an existing ceasefire and demanded a U.S. withdrawal. Iran confirmed receiving a formal U.S. response to its [14-point peace proposal,](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLGOrSAURb8GOwweUO4rKF5Dd1_7SnOE45UZFAOomfv1E-cTptzJyt476_9zfGKIYXv9w5VMrvPokx_LsWdayaUj14InFZxSriFtIwgYuOi5UOMWx67xxjuPnWvIdFrrP3JQHTSLcc5rIXsxad0Dqt5LMXt69E4DIEhogrmrRC8UyE5KaIdhoKnzDyLvvSDFlMBIubaZ9mOKweFWsXzOKTtqXVqbaJZa98LkXwaWgb2uq8X4gW-ijDfBwG50FQY2hpOmmF4M7L3KwPYMrGJgQ8aNX5j5jfBKy50LfhVe87HuhS8pr8ebr6GUkDZ-hhSxUuGOsNAcMjXZ-P0KMYYyaKbEa8UQfw7WX_g8DXwHAAD__4h7h0c) but both sides remain far apart on terms. The Strait carries roughly 20 percent of global oil traffic, keeping energy markets on edge. ★★★
Trump's Approval at Record Low

President Trump's approval rating has fallen to 37 percent -- the lowest of his second term -- with 62 percent disapproving, per a new [Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos poll.](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0LGOtCAUBeCnwU5zQcSxoPgbuvnbLQ3CHYcsAoHr-Pob9xG2OdXJ-ZLz9VyfNsSQ9v_2QF3ptfrs13aWige6fFZq9oPNbrlSyGkVIFQPUw9yTXHlndfeectdh5rP87yMSnLRvTUCV06Bm5SHbV74a4NlkTBty-L5A10X9D0FE0gx8nEUg1IKN-4fiN57QMkk2IiVhorl3GJwNpFt369cHQ4uH13Ub6LS2PiPCcOEua5ruGx7h7RTTiU3umtMmJJjoOAaE-Y2mTAw3TEyYaieR-ltKTV_bOyrpZD21pccIxOmq9qXK8QYmpqZhP2wIf7i9IevPlr8BAAA__9Q7Xlg) The survey lands exactly six months before November's midterm elections. Voters cite the Iran war and economic anxiety as the primary drivers of dissatisfaction. Democrats now hold a five-point advantage on the [congressional generic ballot,](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckDtuwzAQBU9DdTKWH5FWwSKNOqdNKVDk2iZMaQVybSe3D5QjpHnNAG-A-brMl5BL3m6fYUVf-TonSnN77hVXjPSs3MILW1iocqZtVqBsD0MPZt7KLLvkU0xBxg69dM6N2hqpuruPowVMZ7i6NCZn9CAtOFgQRxcwWNNlf1zBAEZpqbU6WWtxkemMmFICNMJAKFj5VHF_LiXHsHFojyvViKdIa1f8nXlvQn8INQk17VQy50gHFGra8N0KMmNtByzhZyF6CDUdXqEmGI4xQk0tf_crbXxvPVN_ox5gBKNh7KpP-zuXkpt1wsBtDbn8ufkfqV5e_QYAAP__UOJ3PA) up from two points in February per the same poll. Two-thirds of Americans say the country is headed in the [wrong direction.](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0MGOniAUBeCnwR1_4MKPumDRpHE3TXddGuRelRTBAI6Zt2_sI8z6JF_OOX8-5g8XYkjbL3eQLW2dMeNcr7PQQT5fpVX3SdUtubSQ0wwCDBdvLvSc4iw7tOjRSd-RlX3fj8poCd1uezOCWXBdsSeltRjAAQxS-xFBvM3QBftQ4i00KKkUvIwxtEgciBBRkGZauEilvQqd1xKDd6m5-nfNxdPL56OLdm_trEz9YDAxmNziE931yRhMv3MMLfjKYGp7KFi5O6g8SuU-X6mVL76TQ0J-l5w2jqGQfzZyt3j-SLere0hby4nBVFsuX0xNAZn6KRW8ByXGsSsWzzvEGKrpmRbb4UL8365948xPC_8CAAD__3WOhhA) With six months remaining, strategists in both parties are watching whether Trump's numbers stabilize -- or keep falling -- before November.
* * *
Dem Distances Themselves From Platner

Michigan Congresswoman Debbie Dingell [refused to endorse](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL1uwyAURp_G3rAAY5wMDF2ypWtH65p7SVD5E-C4j1-lj9DpGz7p6Oh83bc7-ODT4xMimdrdhhm3dpRKkWw-am_wogZ7rt3ntEkuNeML42pLYRMjGrQIwo5kxLqu11krIcen2XcNWonrLJzY3UUsSkrcuXQXody6wOjNG8UXruQs5llOWmvaBV6IEJGTGhSHQLVPlcqxB28hdWjfLldLk81xDObZe2nD_DHI2yBv53lOLv8kOtv7H-QtEnp4r7dP_4DEkCKrVBiSDT5RY-0oJdfOSoCeqLJK7agOLCGrUIjZHCOl3sZqsJw-BN_0Oij-iODDn0X_R7SXkb8BAAD__wTBf8M) Maine Democrat Senate candidate Graham Platner after Platner's past controversial comments about rape surfaced.

★★★

body:
We are writing today to ask you to make a contribution to Elissa Slotkin's campaign committee.
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=2446%2E135344%2ELHULOh)

We are writing today to ask you to make a contribution to Elissa Slotkin's campaign committee.
You may be asking, Elissa just won her Senate race – why are you asking me to contribute again?
First, it goes without saying that Elissa Slotkin won Michigan – and so did Donald Trump.
One of the reasons that happened is because we did better than typical Democrats in the "redder" parts of the state. That is something that has happened consistently in Elissa's previous elections. She might not win them outright, but she "loses better."
Here in Michigan, we have a bunch of big elections this November. Every statewide office is up – Governor, Secretary of State, Attorney General. We have an open Senate seat with Gary Peters' retirement. The entire state senate. And we have U.S. House races that could determine control of the chamber.
But even in other parts of the country, Elissa is getting a lot of requests to join Democrats in tough races campaign trail. And given the importance of this election, she wants to do everything she can to help.
That takes resources. We're not asking for a huge contribution today, just whatever you feel is worth it to help Democrats hold statewide offices, our other Senate seat, and to flip the House.
If lots and lots of people contribute, we can help Elissa play her part.
[**Please use this link to contribute to Elissa Slotkin today. Our average online donation is around $40. Many give more. Some give less. body:
#
**[Peter, is there anything else I can say right now to get you to split $10 between Justice Democrats and our campaign to power our Defend District 9 Fund? We're aiming to raise $100,000 from supporters like you!](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260504-1-jp.8hK82v&refcode=em20260504-37742&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=2&akid=37742%2E1203867%2EFrEIrR)**
**[GIVE $10 OR MORE NOW ››](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260504-1-jp.8hK82v&refcode=em20260504-37742&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=3&akid=37742%2E1203867%2EFrEIrR)**
The Supreme Court’s decision in _Louisiana v. Callais_ destroyed what remained of the landmark Voting Rights Act of 1965. And now, MAGA is using that moment and has set its sights on a new target: **our district.**
Their goal is to erase TN-09 as a majority-Black district because they know we’re standing in the way of their authoritarian plans. And they’re saying it as plain as day.
Senator Marsha Blackburn, who is running to be our state’s next Governor joined the call this week to redraw Tennessee’s congressional maps in order eliminate the state’s one remaining Democratic seat.
Peter, _a_ _nyone_ who is calling for the elimination of other People’s right to representation — for the right of communities to choose their own leaders — should _not_ be in anywhere near power. Not as governor. Not as a senator.
But our district is just one part of a much larger plan. Across the country, the GOP has been laser-focused on making it harder for more People to participate in our democracy. Because they know People are fed up and that _without_ tilting the scales in their favor, they’d lose power.
That’s why we’re building a grassroots Movement strong enough to take them on — not only to save our democracy, but to win the future that our People and neighborhoods deserve.
**[I’m counting on you to join us now and split a $10 donation or more so we can confront this threat head-on with the power of the People.](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260504-1-jp.8hK82v&refcode=em20260504-37742&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=4&akid=37742%2E1203867%2EFrEIrR)**

Justin J. Pearson

I didn’t run for Senate to sit quietly on the sidelines. I’m a mom, a conservative, and a proud Alabamian—and I came to fight for the values that make America strong.

_**Faith. Family. Freedom.**_

The Left is doing _everything_ they can to tear it all down. But I didn’t come to Washington to play games. I came to fight for the people who feel forgotten, overlooked, and ignored.

From securing the border to protecting our kids and defending our way of life—I’m in this for the long haul.

**This fight isn’t easy, but it’s worth it. And I’m not going anywhere.**

Will you stand with me?

I’m humbling myself today because I’ve realized I cannot carry this burden alone. The only way I can see a path forward for our majority—and for President Trump’s agenda—is if my most trusted allies know exactly what we are up against. I’ve written a special note for you. I can only move forward if I know you’re standing with me. Please don’t share this with anyone. God Bless, | | I didn’t run for Senate to sit quietly on the sidelines. I’m a mom, a conservative, and a proud Alabamian—and I came to fight for the values that make America strong. Faith. Family. Freedom. The Left is doing everything they can to tear it all down. But I didn’t come to Washington to play games. I came to fight for the people who feel forgotten, overlooked, and ignored. From securing the border to protecting our kids and defending our way of life—I’m in this for the long haul. This fight isn’t easy, but it’s worth it. And I’m not going anywhere. Will you stand with me? Paid for by Britt for Alabama, Inc. |

body:
Trump-endorsed conservative Julia Letlow heads into final stretch with commanding financial advantage

| | |
---
| | | | [|

| | | | | | FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASEMay 4, 2026[katherine@julialetlow.com](mailto:katherine@julialetlow.com)
**LETLOW RAISES $1.1 MILLION, FLEMING RAISES $23,000 DURING PRE-PRIMARY PERIOD** _Trump-endorsed conservative heads into final stretch with commanding financial advantage_
**BATON ROUGE, LA** – Congresswoman Julia Letlow and aligned entities will report more than $1.1 million raised during the pre-primary reporting period, a commanding show of financial strength as the Trump-endorsed conservative heads into the final stretch of Louisiana's U.S. Senate race. The pre-primary reporting period ran from April 1, 2026 to April 26, 2026.
The Letlow campaign raised $520,000 between April 1 and April 26. Pro-Letlow outside groups raised more than $600,000 over the same period, bringing total resources to over $1.1 million in just 26 days. The Letlow campaign will also report having over $1.6 million cash on hand at the end of the reporting period.
Over the same 26-day window, John Fleming [raised](https://us.list-manage.com/1CnUyVfqxJh?e=95355a072c&c2id=cd64ea42b1b0eeac0fd7d107db75288a) $23,000.
Letlow’s pre-primary haul comes on the heels of an approximately $8 million first quarter and reflects sustained grassroots energy and donor momentum heading into the May 16 Republican primary.
_"Louisianans are showing up for this campaign because they want a senator who stands with President Trump and fights for our families, our values, and the future we owe our children,"_ **said Congresswoman Julia Letlow.** _"I am grateful for every person who has poured into this effort, and I will keep working to earn every vote between now and May 16."_
Learn more at [JuliaLetlow.com](https://us.list-manage.com/KvD22oOKI1g?e=95355a072c&c2id=cd64ea42b1b0eeac0fd7d107db75288a).

subject: What they're doing in Tennessee is exactly why I decided to run

body:
Government isn't about partisan power, it's about helping families.

| | | | |
---
Peter, The Tennessee General Assembly will return for a special session this week. Not to lower your grocery bill. Not to help the farmers dealing with fertilizer costs that are through the roof. Not to do a single thing about the kitchen table issues families across TN-5 are losing sleep over. **They called it to redraw the maps to help MAGA stay in power.** That's it. A special session — the kind you're supposed to call when there's an actual emergency, when people need help — just to protect their own power. To make it harder for your voice to count. To lock in the results they want before you even get a chance to vote. I've said from the beginning that I'm sick of watching Washington spend more time on who's in power than on actually using that power to do something for working families. This is exactly what I was talking about. This is exactly why I decided to run. Gerrymandering isn't an abstract political concept. It's a decision, made by people in a room somewhere, that your vote should matter less. That they should get to choose their voters instead of the other way around. And they're doing it right now, in our state, because they know what's happening in this district. They know we're building something real here, and they are scared of it. That's not going to stop us. clean_body: Government isn't about partisan power, it's about helping families. | | | | | Peter, The Tennessee General Assembly will return for a special session this week. Not to lower your grocery bill. Not to help the farmers dealing with fertilizer costs that are through the roof. Not to do a single thing about the kitchen table issues families across TN-5 are losing sleep over. They called it to redraw the maps to help MAGA stay in power. That's it. A special session — the kind you're supposed to call when there's an actual emergency, when people need help — just to protect their own power. To make it harder for your voice to count. To lock in the results they want before you even get a chance to vote. I've said from the beginning that I'm sick of watching Washington spend more time on who's in power than on actually using that power to do something for working families. This is exactly what I was talking about. This is exactly why I decided to run. Gerrymandering isn't an abstract political concept. It's a decision, made by people in a room somewhere, that your vote should matter less. That they should get to choose their voters instead of the other way around. And they're doing it right now, in our state, because they know what's happening in this district. They know we're building something real here, and they are scared of it. That's not going to stop us. But it does mean the stakes just got higher. ~~ If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your secure donation will go through immediately: | | ~ | ~ | ~ | ~ | The people of Middle Tennessee deserve a representative who's focused on them, not on drawing lines on a map to stay in power. That's not leadership. That's not public service. That's the whole problem. We're going to keep fighting. I hope you're with us. — Chaz | | ---|---|--- About Chaz Molder Chaz Molder is the Mayor of Columbia, Tennessee, serving since 2019 and re-elected in 2022. A Columbia native and graduate of the University of Tennessee and the University of Memphis Law School, he returned home to build a career in law and public service. As mayor, he founded the Columbia Mayor’s Youth Council to promote civic engagement among young people and emphasizes the importance of being present and responsive to the community. | | | ~~ Click~~ to receive fewer emails. | | Hi, I’m not going to sugarcoat the new SCOTUS ruling in _Louisiana v. Callais._ It dismantled one of the most important protections that kept politicians from rigging voting maps for their own power and silencing voters of color in our diverse country. And this decision is not an accident — it’s the endgame of a decades‐long strategy by Republican politicians and billionaire donors to dismantle our voting rights, advance an agenda of white supremacy, block our votes, and lock the people out of power, especially targeting the South where most Black Americans live. So as we fight back, we have to zoom out and take that entire picture into account. Last month, when the Fair Fight team convened for an all-staff retreat, we got to review the broad current landscape of threats to voting rights, discuss lessons learned from recent fights, and map out our strategies to protect the freedom to vote. And I got to reflect on how this whole pro-democracy movement — which you help power — is more than ready to meet this incredibly difficult moment. We founded Fair Fight to tackle times like these. After Georgia voters faced significant difficulties in the 2018 elections, we launched this organization to help make sure every eligible voter can register, cast their ballot, and have it counted — always rooted in and focused on the South but with a national purview. **When the freedom to vote is under threat, we’re there to defend it** — powering critical voter protection efforts, electing Democracy Champions to offices that play major roles in elections, and exposing and pushing back against attempts at voter suppression. So even though our democracy is under enormous strain right now, I’m confident that together we can build a deeper and broader movement that will rise to this challenge. But I want to be straightforward with you about what lies ahead. Here are some of the key fights we’re facing, and how the pro-democracy movement plans to deliver victories for voters. _**The aftermath of _Louisiana v. Callais: _**_
_The Supreme Court has gutted another key plank of the Voting Rights Act, threatening to decimate fair representation for communities of color and let Republicans entrench one-party rule._ _But our communities have never won anything by giving up, so we intend to use all of our tools to fight back. We have more power together — and when we come together to vote, to advocate and organize, working with a powerful coalition of litigators, leaders and allies across the political spectrum — we can slow, stop and mitigate the bad. We can still elect leaders who work for strong public schools, good jobs, and affordable healthcare and housing._ _It’s time to generate massive resistance against attempts to rig maps for the 2026 elections. And we’ll continue working to generate massive turnout in November to combat the MAGA power grab._ _The pro-democracy movement isn’t out of options. Blue‐state leaders can redraw maps to respond. State legislators can fight against discriminatory and unfair voting maps and file pro-voting rights bills. Communities can organize, raise awareness, and pressure lawmakers to reject discriminatory maps._ _Remember: if your vote didn’t matter — they wouldn’t be working so hard to take it away._ _**The 2026 elections in Georgia, including this month’s State Supreme Court elections:**_
_We’ve endorsed two Democracy Champions for the bench — Jen Jordan and Miracle Rankin — so we can add pro-voter, pro-freedom voices to a body with authority over elections challenges and state constitutional questions (including reproductive rights)._ _And through November, we’ll fight to flip the State House from red to blue, keep an election denier from winning the Secretary of State’s race, win critical local elections that determine who oversees elections, and re-elect Senator Jon Ossoff._ _**Trump’s executive order on mail voting (and what else he may try to push):**_
_Our team has kept close tabs on the election deniers who’ve drafted executive order language for Trump, and on which pieces are already reflected in his attempt to restrict mail voting. That order is already getting challenged in the courts. By continuing to stay on top of new ways Trump could try to threaten voting rights, we help make sure the pro-democracy ecosystem is ready to respond to those measures as well._ [**No matter what comes next, your support helps make sure we’re able to respond to new threats right away and continue protecting the freedom to vote. clean_body: A message about where we stand | | | Hi, I’m not going to sugarcoat the new SCOTUS ruling in Louisiana v. Callais. It dismantled one of the most important protections that kept politicians from rigging voting maps for their own power and silencing voters of color in our diverse country. And this decision is not an accident — it’s the endgame of a decades‐long strategy by Republican politicians and billionaire donors to dismantle our voting rights, advance an agenda of white supremacy, block our votes, and lock the people out of power, especially targeting the South where most Black Americans live. So as we fight back, we have to zoom out and take that entire picture into account. Last month, when the Fair Fight team convened for an all-staff retreat, we got to review the broad current landscape of threats to voting rights, discuss lessons learned from recent fights, and map out our strategies to protect the freedom to vote. And I got to reflect on how this whole pro-democracy movement — which you help power — is more than ready to meet this incredibly difficult moment. We founded Fair Fight to tackle times like these. After Georgia voters faced significant difficulties in the 2018 elections, we launched this organization to help make sure every eligible voter can register, cast their ballot, and have it counted — always rooted in and focused on the South but with a national purview. When the freedom to vote is under threat, we’re there to defend it — powering critical voter protection efforts, electing Democracy Champions to offices that play major roles in elections, and exposing and pushing back against attempts at voter suppression. So even though our democracy is under enormous strain right now, I’m confident that together we can build a deeper and broader movement that will rise to this challenge. But I want to be straightforward with you about what lies ahead. Here are some of the key fights we’re facing, and how the pro-democracy movement plans to deliver victories for voters. The aftermath of Louisiana v. Callais: The Supreme Court has gutted another key plank of the Voting Rights Act, threatening to decimate fair representation for communities of color and let Republicans entrench one-party rule. But our communities have never won anything by giving up, so we intend to use all of our tools to fight back. We have more power together — and when we come together to vote, to advocate and organize, working with a powerful coalition of litigators, leaders and allies across the political spectrum — we can slow, stop and mitigate the bad. We can still elect leaders who work for strong public schools, good jobs, and affordable healthcare and housing. It’s time to generate massive resistance against attempts to rig maps for the 2026 elections. And we’ll continue working to generate massive turnout in November to combat the MAGA power grab. The pro-democracy movement isn’t out of options. Blue‐state leaders can redraw maps to respond. State legislators can fight against discriminatory and unfair voting maps and file pro-voting rights bills. Communities can organize, raise awareness, and pressure lawmakers to reject discriminatory maps. Remember: if your vote didn’t matter — they wouldn’t be working so hard to take it away. The 2026 elections in Georgia, including this month’s State Supreme Court elections: We’ve endorsed two Democracy Champions for the bench — Jen Jordan and Miracle Rankin — so we can add pro-voter, pro-freedom voices to a body with authority over elections challenges and state constitutional questions (including reproductive rights). And through November, we’ll fight to flip the State House from red to blue, keep an election denier from winning the Secretary of State’s race, win critical local elections that determine who oversees elections, and re-elect Senator Jon Ossoff. Trump’s executive order on mail voting (and what else he may try to push): Our team has kept close tabs on the election deniers who’ve drafted executive order language for Trump, and on which pieces are already reflected in his attempt to restrict mail voting. That order is already getting challenged in the courts.
